coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Domestic work abroad is regulated via overseas-employment law (Proc. 923/2016 repealed and replaced by Proc. 1389/2025 per a Reporter/EBR summary; a Kuwait domestic-worker MoU ratified by Proc. 1337/2024). Buyer is the sending agency, not households. No household-employer registration duty found. See candidate on overseas employment agencies.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Ethiopian scrap-metal licensing law or register found in English search (results were Kenya, Zambia, UK). Nothing actionable; Amharic search not run.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Ethiopia-specific second-hand or pawn register found; only the general Addis Trade Bureau licence regime. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Gold buying is channelled to the National Bank of Ethiopia (premium raised to 35%; officials want to cut out intermediary suppliers). No found record-keeping or reporting regime for jewellers. One weak candidate recorded.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Nothing on dismantler or used-parts licensing found; only general trade licensing and annual renewal.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: 2014 live animals marketing law (licensed traders, registered markets) and a draft slaughter/traceability proclamation (status unconfirmed). Nothing new beyond K11 (ETLITS).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Study evidence of weak regulation and ~60-80% illegal slaughter in Addis; a Ministry of Agriculture draft proclamation would require sourcing from registered farm/market and slaughter in abattoirs (enactment unconfirmed). Weak candidate recorded.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No search spent; K05 already covers honey exporter traceability.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Proclamation 728/2011 governs veterinary drugs; Reg. 325/2014 sets fees; Ethiopian Agricultural Authority reportedly moved applications to an e-service system (Jan 2025 directive, per a 2025 report). Retail shop duties not confirmed.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Resources Management Proc. 197/2000 and Council of Ministers Reg. 115/2005 require permits, certification of drillers and drilling-completion reports to the supervising body. Current licensing process and any replacing law unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Solid Waste Management Proc. 513/2007 lets private operators and MSEs hold collection permits; Addis zones assigned per enterprise. Nothing found on septic truck licensing.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Ethiopian Construction Authority draft directive (Fortune, 27 Sep 2025) would license elevator installers, maintainers and independent inspection firms who issue clearance reports. No deadline, finalisation unconfirmed. Boiler and pressure-vessel rules not found.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No dedicated search; only the general water-permit regime surfaced under category 10.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Fertilizer Proc. 137/1998 requires a competence certificate for wholesale or retail; Pesticide Decree 20/1990 (registration). Whether the Agricultural Authority now licenses dealers, and any 2024-25 change, not confirmed.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Overseas employment is under Proc. 1389/2025 (replacing 923/2016 as amended 1246/2021): agency capital 5m-20m Br and USD 50k-250k security deposit tiers (Oct 2025 Ministry of Labour and Skills directive), an Ethiopian Labour Migration Information System, and a 2024 licensing backlog of 100+ applicants. Candidate recorded.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No search spent; K04 covers edir ledgers. See CSO candidate for the reporting regime that may apply to associations.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: CSO Proclamation 1113/2019: annual renewal with general-assembly-approved audit report; Authority revoked 1,718 licences in 2024 for missing reports. Candidate recorded. Halal supervision not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Addis Transport Bureau is drafting ride-hailing rules (terminals, mandatory GPS, vehicle identification); 44 registered ride-hailing companies, only 10-15 active. Annual vehicle inspection regime and minibus association rules not confirmed. Weak candidate recorded.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: 2025 income tax amendment (Proc. 1395/2025) dissolves Category C into B, taxing sub-2m Br turnover individuals on gross sales at 2-5%; Addis business licences must be renewed yearly (Proc. 686/2014 rules; only 72% of 384,000 complied in the 2025 fiscal year per a Trade Bureau report). Forex bureaus under NBE Directive FXD/01/2024 (5 licensed Oct 2024). Candidates recorded.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Private kindergartens and schools are evaluated and de-licensed by Addis education quality authority (824 evaluated, 11 revoked in 2021); Directive 206 of 1994/95 outdated per a 2022 parliamentary committee. Driving schools, day care, tattoo, small food producers and hunting outfitters: nothing found, not separately searched.

candidates.category: 35. E-invoicing and sales-register mandate (Ministry of Revenue Directive 1142/2026)
candidates.existing: EDICOM, Odoo partners and ETTA Zoorya per earlier study notes and this pass

candidates.name: E-invoicing (Directive 1142/2026) and sales-register migration
candidates.trigger: Ministry of Revenue Electronic Invoicing System Administration Directive 1142/2026 (published 1 Jul 2026); large taxpayers targeted by end-Dec 2026; no rollout schedule yet.
candidates.unchecked: Nothing re-checked, per the contract.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: PEA (federal) enforces station stock/inventory reporting and fuel-truck delivery reporting, with licence revocation threats; Telebirr-data audit of 225 stations led to suspensions; March 2026 emergency fuel-conservation directive; a 2026 draft directive would make privileged institutions file monthly fuel-use reports. Reporting appears to run through state/Ethio telecom systems. No LPG-specific rule found. See candidates C06 and C13.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: ECTA Directive 1106/2025 (capital to Birr 15m/20m, ECTA-certified lab, one taster per exporter): few buyers, large firms. Government built ECTMS traceability platform (handed to ECTA 27 Mar 2026), which overlaps K03. MoTRI Directive 1115/2025 routes oilseed/pulse export payments through ECX; sector in turmoil in early 2026. ECX warehousing is the state EACWSE. No warehouse-operator licence rule found. Nothing new beyond K03 for coffee.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Federal Cooperative Commission issued a 2024 financial-services standard directive for about 23,000 cooperatives (deposit/credit rules). A draft cooperative proclamation amendment (non-member 10% share, mandatory annual audit and general assembly) is in parliament, not confirmed enacted. SACCOs are supervised by general cooperative offices. See C03.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: CBHI is run by the Ethiopian Health Insurance Agency in 1,063 woredas; SHI for the formal sector is still pending. MoH Ethiopian Healthcare Accreditation Program (EHAP) primary-care and diagnostic-centre requirements published 2025, and hospital standard ES 7191:2025 was out for comment. Claims-submission rules for private clinics not found. See C08.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: EFDA Narcotic and Psychotropic Medicine Control Directive 1121 (Dec 2025) replaces the serial prescription-pad regime with supply-chain recordkeeping, reporting, stock audits and higher penalties; a study found only 23.9% prescription compliance in pharmacies. EFDA runs eRIS (i-License) for premises licensing. Precursor chemicals not searched. See C04.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No comprehensive private security law found (older thesis); licensing apparently by the Federal Police Commission (unverified blog). Overseas private employment agencies are licensed by the Ministry of Labour and Skills (Reg. 282/2013 fees; ILO 2025-26 briefs; new Overseas Employment Proclamation). Cleaning agencies not found. See C11.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Contractors: graded licences (Grade 10 to 1) renewed every calendar year with 3 years of audited accounts, tax clearance and association membership; late renewal inside 3 years costs 50% extra (older, undated sources, federal). Mining: draft bill would stop regional states licensing artisanal miners; gold goes to NBE with a premium reportedly ending end-2026 (unconfirmed); mass licence revocations. See C09 and C14.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Real Estate Development and Immovable Property Marketing and Valuation Proclamation (reported as No. 1357/2024) sets broker licensing standards; Proclamation 1388/2025 opens residential ownership to foreigners. No source found on whether brokers or notaries must report to the FIS (AML); a DNFBP search returned nothing on Ethiopia. See C10 and C15.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Addis Ababa Regulation 204/2026: 5% municipal tax on room tariff from 19 Jun 2026 (Fortune) with mandatory guest register, an 'Accommodation Municipal Tax' invoice line, monthly or quarterly filing, 5% per month late penalty, and Tourism Commission accreditation renewal tied to a tax-compliance letter. About 500 bookable hotels with over 25,000 rooms, many not ready. This is the strongest lead. See C01.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Coffee: K03 and the state ECTMS platform. Sesame/pulses/oilseeds: pre-registration, sales-contract and 40-day export rules (2024), Directive 1115/2025 payment routing via ECX, price matching. Fish and timber not searched (budget). See C05.

coverage.category: 31. Addis Ababa city revenue regulations (hotel lodging tax)
coverage.found: Covered in 29 and C01.

coverage.category: 32. Residential rental and lease registration (Addis Ababa Revenues Bureau directive)
coverage.found: Fortune (12 Jul 2026): directive targets about 500,000 landlords. Every lease must be registered and rent paid through bank or digital channels. Most landlords are in presumptive Category C (flat 35% deduction, then progressive brackets). Surcharges of 5% to 25% of monthly rent for unregistered leases, vacancy penalties. See C02.

coverage.category: 33. EV charging and energy licensing (PEA directive)
coverage.found: PEA EV-charging directive approved by Jan 2025: station licensing (existing operators within 6 months), tariff approval, 50 km spacing. Tiny market now. See C07.

coverage.category: 34. Financial-sector small institutions (NBE microfinance and agent banking)
coverage.found: NBE tightening MFI audits (Oct 2025; 53 MFIs), MFI IT directive MFI/33/2022 with interoperability, capital-market registration extension requested (Mar 2026). Use of Agents Directive (2020) is being split for mobile money agents. Large institutions and few buyers; no small-business duty found. See C12.

coverage.category: 35. E-invoicing and sales-register mandate (Ministry of Revenue Directive 1142/2026)
coverage.found: Directive 1142/2026 (1 Jul 2026) makes compliant electronic sales recording mandatory for taxpayers who keep books, with no rollout schedule yet; large taxpayers targeted by end-Dec 2026. Same buyer and duty as K01; ETTA Zoorya (certified POS) is an existing local product.

coverage.category: 36. Real estate and property law 2024-2025 (Proclamations 1357/2024, 1388/2025)
coverage.found: Covered in 28 and C10, C15.

coverage.category: 37. Export commodity payment controls (MoTRI Directive 1115/2025, ECX)
coverage.found: Covered in 22/30 and C05.
